run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T12:59:14Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for service_name=frontend-proxy is firing because that service's Envoy ingress returns HTTP 503 to a small fraction of requests. At the alert's start instant (2026-11-15T12:59:14Z) the rate of STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on frontend-proxy's server span 'ingress' (metric traces_span_metrics_calls_total) was exactly 0.011111111111111112 /s, which is the value in the alert annotation, against an ingress span rate of 12.44/s of non-error spans — i.e. roughly one error per 90 s, about 0.06% of ingress spans (15.21 error vs 27,090 non-error spans over the 77-minute window). The 503s are not app-level errors: Envoy's access log records them with response flag upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} against upstream host 'frontend', with 0 bytes received, and the failed requests never produce a frontend span — the frontend (Next.js) side terminated the TCP connection without processing the request. The single frontend pod (frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t) is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, 61% of its memory limit and zero error spans of its own, but its container is pinned at its 100m CPU limit with 30-35% CFS throttling throughout the window. That CPU saturation of the upstream is the leading explanation for the connection terminations; an Envoy/Node HTTP keep-alive reuse race is an equally plausible but unverified alternative. Causality between the throttling and the 503 UC resets is not proven by the available evidence.

claims.text: At 2026-11-15T12:59:14Z, rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m]) = 0.011111111111111112 per second, while the STATUS_CODE_UNSET ingress rate was 12.437037037037037/s; this reproduces the alert annotation's current value of 0.01111111111111111. The client span 'router frontend egress' had 0 error rate at that instant.

Over the full 77-minute query window (2026-11-15T11:59:14Z-13:17:05Z) frontend-proxy recorded 15.211 error spans and 27,090.254 non-error (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) spans on span_name='ingress', i.e. about 0.06% error share; all errors are on 'ingress' and the 'router frontend egress' error series is 0.

The frontend-proxy errors are 503 responses: sampled error traces show a frontend-proxy span 'ingress' with status tags error=true, http.status_code=503, otel.status_code=ERROR, whose child span 'router frontend egress' (service frontend-proxy) carries error="true" and http.status_code="0"; the corresponding load-generator client spans (e.g. operation GET, user_browse_product, user_add_to_cart) record http.status_code=503. Error traces in the sample span 12:34:31Z to 12:53:24Z.

The frontend-proxy container's Envoy access log names the upstream failure: e.g. at 2026-11-15T12:34:31.225Z "GET /api/data/?contextKeys=telescopes HTTP/1.1" 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}, upstream host 'frontend', 0 bytes received; at 12:41:19.362Z the same flag for GET /api/products/66VCHSJNUP; at 12:52:35.248Z for GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO and 12:52:35.281Z for GET /; at 12:53:23.712Z for GET /api/products/1YMWWN1N4O. In the same 12:52:30-12:53:30 window a normal request POST /api/cart returned 200 via_upstream.

The failed requests never reach the frontend application: whole-trace fetch of trace 006109e39dbc3e0e38ea35e8110e2b5c (503 at 12:52:35Z) contains only 4 spans (load-generator user_browse_product and GET, frontend-proxy ingress 503 and router frontend egress) with no frontend service span, and trace 763e156025c14f131f4d556cfffccada contains a 503 ingress attempt with no frontend span plus an immediately retried attempt that produced the normal chain frontend 'POST /api/cart' (200) -> 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' -> grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem -> cart spans.

The upstream is the single-replica frontend deployment: k8s Service 'frontend' maps port 8080 to targetPort 8080, deployment frontend has 1 desired/1 ready/1 available replica, and its only pod is frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t on node i-029c97e90b3730286, phase Running, Ready condition True, container restartCount 0, container started 2026-11-15T12:20:18Z. The frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bf4lq is likewise Running/Ready with restartCount 0 (started 12:20:21Z).

The frontend service reports no errors of its own: every traces_span_metrics_calls_total series with service_name="frontend" and status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR" (GET, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, POST, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/cart|/api/checkout|/api/data, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem|GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, tcp.connect) evaluates to 0 over the 65-minute window, while frontend-proxy 'ingress' carries 13.24-15.21 errors per evaluation. Across all services the only other error series returned are flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream spans of ad, fraud-detection and recommendation (2.04-5.11 per evaluation).

The frontend container is pinned at its CPU limit: its Deployment sets limits cpu=100m / memory=200Mi and requests cpu=50m / memory=100Mi (no readiness or liveness probe, containerPort 8080); the kube-state-metrics derived limit for pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t is 0.1 core (frontend-proxy: 0.03 core). Measured container CPU use was 0.056-0.108 core and the CFS throttled-period ratio was 0.306-0.349 for the frontend pod, versus 0.011-0.073 for frontend-proxy, across 2026-11-15T12:34-13:14.

The frontend pod is not memory-pressured: container_memory_working_set_bytes for pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t was 128,442,368 bytes at 2026-11-15T13:16:00Z against a 200Mi limit, and it carries no restarts or last termination state.

The condition is continuous rather than a single burst: per-evaluation increase of frontend-proxy ingress error spans over 300s ranged from 1.11 to 5.56 between the first returned sample (2026-11-15T12:36:14Z) and the last (13:16:14Z), while non-error ingress spans were 957-3,888 per 300s. Frontend load at 13:16Z was 16.66 server spans/s, 12.88 client spans/s and 8.27 internal spans/s.

Only a small share of frontend spans is slow: the fraction of frontend spans above 1000 ms was 0.00557-0.00607 over the last three 300s-lookback evaluations ending 2026-11-15T13:14Z. No earlier baseline exists in this Prometheus, so no latency trend can be claimed.

Leading cause: the 503s originate at the frontend upstream, not at the proxy. Envoy's upstream host 'frontend' terminated the TCP connection before any response byte was received (flag upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}), the frontend application never produced a span for the failed requests, and the single frontend pod's container is saturated at its 100m CPU limit with 30-35% CFS throttling, so the Next.js/Node server plausibly abandons or fails to service pooled connections under CPU starvation. The evidence shows the upstream-side termination and the frontend CPU saturation, but does not by itself prove that throttling produced the resets.

Alternative cause not excluded: an Envoy-to-frontend HTTP/1.1 keep-alive reuse race (Envoy reusing a pooled upstream connection that the frontend closed, e.g. Node keepAliveTimeout versus the Envoy cluster's upstream idle timeout) would produce exactly the observed upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} 503s at a low rate (~1 per 1,100 requests), with the request never reaching the application. The frontend-proxy Envoy cluster configuration was not readable in this Run, so this cannot be confirmed or refuted.

The frontend app itself looks healthy on its own signals: zero STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans across all of its operations for 65 minutes, no restarts, Ready, and memory at 61% of its limit. This argues against a crash, OOM, application-level exception or a failing frontend dependency being the visible cause, and it means the 503s are a transport-level symptom, not an app-reported failure.

The frontend CPU throttling level is flat across the window (0.306 -> 0.349 throttled-period ratio from 12:34 to 13:14) while the 5-minute error count fluctuates between 0 and 5.56, so the observed data does not show a correlation between throttling intensity and error bursts; this weakens, without disproving, the CPU-saturation mechanism for the resets.

Pod crash / OOM / rollout of the frontend or frontend-proxy as the cause of these 503s is rejected: both pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0, no previous container instance existed to read, container start times are 12:20:18Z and 12:20:21Z (before the alert), the frontend container's lastState is empty, and memory is well below its limit.

Since ~1 in 1,100 requests is a 503 UC, compare the frontend-proxy Envoy cluster for upstream 'frontend' (upstream idle_timeout / max_requests_per_connection, any retry policy) against the frontend's Node keep-alive timeout, and set Envoy's upstream idle timeout below the upstream keep-alive timeout so stale pooled connections are not reused; enabling a retry for upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on idempotent requests would also mask the user-visible 503s.

Raise the frontend container CPU limit (currently 100m with 50m request) or reduce its SSR/API load: measured use equals the limit and 30-35% of CFS periods are throttled, so there is no CPU headroom for the ~16.7 server spans/s it serves; re-check whether the frontend-proxy 503 UC rate falls afterwards. Adding a readiness probe to the frontend deployment would also give a health signal it currently lacks.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate rule definition could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no data (status no_data) both by rule_name and unfiltered, so the exact expression, window and for-duration behind the 12:59:14Z start are unknown; the alert value was matched empirically from traces_span_metrics_calls_total.

No Prometheus samples exist before ~2026-11-15T12:34Z for these series, so the onset of the 503s is unknown and the alert start (12:59:14Z) cannot be tied to any observed change; errors are already present in the first returned sample.

The frontend container's logs could not be read: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t returned 0 bytes/0 lines for 12:30-13:17Z (no_data) and no previous instance exists, so the upstream-side reason for the connection termination is unknown.

frontend-proxy logs were readable only through about 2026-11-15T12:54:09Z (4 MiB read limit reached) and the 13:14:30-13:17:05Z window returned 0 lines, so the 503 log lines after 12:54Z were not read; whether later errors carry the same upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} flag is unknown.

Jaeger trace data ends around 2026-11-15T12:52-12:54Z (source_end_at of the trace results), so no traces cover the later part of the incident window and the sampled spans are not a complete trace graph or a failure rate.

No non-Normal Kubernetes events were returned for namespace otel-demo (events query no_data; 78 items processed inside the window), so any Evicted/Unhealthy/kubelet events during the window are unknown.

Kubernetes state metrics for otel-demo are largely absent from Prometheus: kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready and kube_pod_container_resource_limits returned no data, so deployment readiness over time could not be verified and resource limits had to be read from the Deployment object and the kube-state-metrics recording rule.
The frontend-proxy Envoy configuration (upstream cluster idle timeouts, keep-alive settings, retry policy) was not accessible, so the keep-alive race hypothesis cannot be confirmed or excluded.
The change-history integration is not available in this Run, so no deployment/configuration change can be correlated with the incident.
next_steps: Read the actual RequestErrorRate rule (query/window/for) from the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule files to confirm the alert semantics: it appears to fire on any non-zero absolute error-span rate, which one sporadic 503 every ~90 s satisfies.

Inspect the frontend-proxy Envoy cluster definition for upstream 'frontend' (idle_timeout, max_requests_per_connection, retry_policy) and the frontend's Node keepAliveTimeout/headersTimeout, then align the timeouts and/or add a retry for connection-termination resets.

Collect and inspect the frontend container's stdout logs around the 503 timestamps (12:34:31Z, 12:41:19Z, 12:42:15Z, 12:42:58Z, 12:49:07Z, 12:52:35Z, 12:52:35Z, 12:53:23Z, plus later ones) to see whether the Next.js server logs aborted/reset sockets.
Increase the frontend container CPU limit (or reduce load) and re-measure the frontend-proxy 503 UC rate to test the CPU-saturation hypothesis.
Add an Envoy access-log field for the upstream transport failure reason and a frontend readiness probe, so the next occurrence yields upstream-side diagnostics.
